production.waterSource: Water used to reduce new make spirit is sourced from deep wells; the distillery describes its production water as being drawn from ancient rock formations.
production.malt: The distillery grows heritage barley on the Scully family's farm and uses both malted and unmalted barley for its single pot still production.
production.fermentation: Clonakilty states that fermentation is deliberately lengthened to allow its yeast more time to develop flavour; an exact duration is not disclosed in the verified first-party sources reviewed.
production.stills: Its single pot still whiskey is triple-distilled; the distillery's customer-facing technical material does not publish still capacities or condenser geometry in the verified source set reviewed.
production.maturation: Whiskey is matured in oak casks in the Atlantic coastal environment; the distillery also highlights a gradual 'gentle cut' approach when adding water to spirit.

houseCharacter: Clonakilty's house approach centres on long fermentation, triple distillation and the use of both malted and unmalted barley in its pot still whiskey. Those choices are designed to create a lighter, sweeter spirit while retaining grain and fermentation character. Coastal maturation and the use of family-grown heritage barley reinforce the distillery's emphasis on local raw materials and provenance.
cask23Narrative: Clonakilty is a County Cork distillery built around a strong farm-to-whiskey identity. Its pot still spirit combines malted and unmalted barley, extended fermentation and triple distillation, giving customers a useful contrast to heavier double-distilled styles. The distillery's coastal location and use of deep-well water and family-grown barley make it especially relevant for anyone interested in how Irish whiskey can express both production method and place.
